title: Goldman Sachs Resets S&P 500 Price Target - Yahoo Finance
text: Goldman Sachs Resets S&P 500 Price Target Nauman Khan March 16, 2026 1 min read GS +0.53% ^GSPC -0.38% This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Goldman Sachs (GS) strategists said the U.S. equity market may still have room to rise, projecting the S&P 500 could reach about 7,600 by the end of 2026 as corporate earnings expand and economic growth remains steady, according to a weekly strategy report released Monday. The bank expects earnings for companies in the index to reach about $309 per share in 2026 and around $342 in 2027. That outlook implies annual growth of roughly 12% and 10%, respectively, which strategists say could support an index return of about 14% from recent levels. Warning! Technology companies are expected to remain the largest driver of profit expansion. Goldman Sachs estimates the information technology sector could contribute about $92 per share to index earnings in 2026, rising to roughly $109 in 2027, up from about $70 in 2025. Financials, healthcare and communication services are also expected to contribute to overall profit growth, though at a slower pace. Valuations appear elevated but still near historical norms, with the index trading at about 21 times forward earnings. The report also noted increasing market concentration, with the ten largest companies accounting for roughly 39% of total market capitalization and about 31% of overall earnings.
